title: Euro breaks below $1.10 as French election risk builds; three banks see $1.08 next
body: With short positioning this stretched, the euro is vulnerable to sharp short-covering rallies even if the trend stays lower. A credible French budget or a soft US inflation reading would be the likeliest triggers. On the downside, the $1.08 to $1.09 area is the next focus, where the bank forecasts and options-market risk sit. The spread between French and German bonds is the gauge to watch: if it stays contained, the move remains mainly a dollar story, and if it widens, the French element takes over. A firm dollar also keeps USD/JPY pressing against Tokyo's intervention zone near 160. --- The euro is caught between French politics and a hawkish Fed, and forecasters see $1.08 next, though positioning is now crowded enough to make the next bounce a sharp one.

title: Barclays: Back-to-back Fed hikes give the dollar staying power that a jumbo 50bp move wouldn't
body: The focus for the dollar shifts from how big the December hike will be to how long the hiking continues. That leans toward front-end Treasury yields staying high into the first quarter. It's a constructive backdrop for the dollar against lower-yielding currencies, although intervention risk near 160 limits the upside in USD/JPY. Gold faces the same headwind it has struggled with all year, as longer-lasting high US rates raise the cost of holding it. Freight and diesel costs are a direct channel from oil to US core inflation, so oil prices now feed straight into Fed pricing. --- Barclays says the dollar's strength comes from how long the Fed keeps hiking, not how big any single move is, and two quarter-point steps do that job better than one jumbo hike. title: Japan's Consumer Prices Edge Higher in October, Breaking September Stall
body: Japan's consumer inflation picked up modestly in October 2026, with the Consumer Price Index (CPI, n.s.a) rising 0.8% month-over-month, according to data updated on 19 November 2026. This marks a clear shift from September 2026, when prices were flat and the index recorded 0.0% on a month-over-month basis. The latest reading indicates that price growth has resumed after a temporary pause in September, when the previous comparison period showed no change from the month before. On a month-over-month basis, October's 0.8% increase reflects renewed upward pressure in consumer prices compared with the stagnation seen in the prior month. For analysts and investors tracking Japan's inflation dynamics, the October data suggests that the disinflationary lull in September was short-lived. title: Japan's October CPI Ticks Up to 2.3% YoY, Signaling Mild Re-Acceleration in Inflation
body: Japan's national Consumer Price Index (CPI) rose 2.3% year-over-year in October 2026, edging higher from September's 2.1% annual gain. The data, updated on 19 November 2026, indicate a modest re-acceleration in inflationary pressures after a slight cooling in the previous month. Both the current and previous readings are measured on a year-over-year basis, comparing price levels in each month to the same month a year earlier. September's 2.1% increase reflected conditions relative to September of the prior year, while October's 2.3% print captures the change versus October a year ago. The uptick suggests that, despite some earlier signs of easing, consumer prices in Japan continue to climb at a rate above the 2% level often watched by markets and policymakers. Investors and analysts are likely to scrutinize whether this upward move marks the start of a more sustained inflation trend or simply a minor fluctuation around the 2% zone. The October data will feed into expectations for Japan's near-term monetary policy stance and assessments of how firmly inflation is taking hold in the domestic economy. Investors and policymakers will be watching whether this incremental acceleration in core inflation marks the start of a more sustained trend or remains a mild overshoot. title: Fed Reserve Balances Edge Back Above $3 Trillion, Signaling Slight Liquidity Uptick
body: Reserve balances with Federal Reserve Banks in the United States have nudged higher, returning above the $3 trillion mark, according to the latest data update on 19 November 2026. The indicator rose from $2.969 trillion previously to $3.001 trillion, marking a modest increase in bank reserves held at the Federal Reserve. The move suggests a slight easing in overall liquidity conditions within the U.S. banking system, as reserve balances reflect the funds that depository institutions hold on account at the Fed. While the change is relatively small in absolute terms, the shift back over the $3 trillion threshold will be closely watched by market participants monitoring the interplay between Federal Reserve operations, money market dynamics, and banking-system liquidity. Analysts will now be looking at subsequent readings to determine whether this uptick represents the start of a more sustained build-up in reserves or a short-term fluctuation around current levels. For the moment, the latest figure underscores that excess liquidity in the financial system remains substantial by historical standards. title: Fed's Balance Sheet Edges Lower to $6.74 Trillion, Signaling Continued Quantitative Tightening
body: The U.S. Federal Reserve's balance sheet declined slightly to $6.741 trillion, according to data updated on 19 November 2026. The latest reading marks a modest decrease from the previous level of $6.759 trillion, underscoring the central bank's ongoing effort to reduce the size of its asset holdings. The incremental drawdown in the balance sheet is consistent with a measured approach to quantitative tightening, as the Fed allows securities to mature without full reinvestment. While the move is relatively small in absolute terms, such shifts are closely monitored by investors for signals about longer-term liquidity conditions and the central bank's stance on withdrawing pandemic-era support from the financial system. title: South Korea's Producer Inflation Eases Slightly in October, PPI Slows to 7.2% YoY
body: South Korea's producer price inflation showed a modest deceleration in October 2026, signaling a slight easing of upstream price pressures in the economy. The Producer Price Index (PPI) rose 7.2% year-over-year in October, down from a 7.6% year-over-year increase recorded in September 2026. Both figures represent annual comparisons, with the October reading measuring price changes relative to October a year earlier, and the September figure comparing to the same month a year before. The data, updated on 19 November 2026, indicate that while producer prices in South Korea remain elevated on an annual basis, the gradual slowdown in the PPI could point to a tentative softening in cost pressures for businesses going forward. For markets and policymakers, the easing from 7.6% to 7.2% year-over-year may be viewed as an early sign that producer-level inflation could be past its peak, though the still-strong pace of annual increases suggests inflation risks remain present in the production side of the economy. title: PBOC is expected to set the USD/CNY reference rate at 6.6731 – Reuters estimate
body: The People's Bank of China is due to set the daily USD/CNY reference rate at around 0115 GMT (2115 US Eastern time), a fixing that remains one of the most closely watched signals in Asian foreign exchange markets. China operates a managed floating exchange rate system, under which the renminbi (yuan) is allowed to trade within a prescribed band around a central reference rate, or midpoint, set each trading day by the PBOC. The current trading band permits the currency to move plus or minus 2% from the official midpoint during onshore trading hours. Each morning, the PBOC determines the midpoint based on a range of inputs. These include the previous day's closing price, movements in major currencies, particularly the US dollar, broader international FX conditions, and domestic economic considerations such as capital flows, growth momentum and financial stability objectives. The midpoint is not a purely mechanical calculation, allowing policymakers discretion to guide market expectations. Once the midpoint is announced, onshore USD/CNY is free to trade within the allowable band. If market pressures push the yuan toward either edge of that range, the central bank may step in to smooth volatility. Intervention can take the form of direct buying or selling of yuan, adjustments to liquidity conditions, or guidance through state-owned banks. As a result, the daily fixing is often interpreted as a policy signal rather than just a technical reference point.

Risk teams may now price that dependency into collateral settings more explicitly. --- It was a heavy day for crypto: Ethereum consolidates around recent lows --- Threshold never ran short of Bitcoin, but for 11 days its token holders couldn't get any of it back. Summary: Threshold Network suspended tBTC redemptions from Oct. 30 to Nov. 10. Its Nov. 18 post-mortem calls it an operational and security failure, not a reserve shortfall. Bridge wallets held about 4,320 BTC against roughly 4,185 tBTC in circulation, a surplus of around 135 BTC. There were two causes: a fault in how the bridge accounted for deposits, and a security issue tied to a Linux kernel flaw that took some signing operators offline. Each wallet needs a majority of its signers to move funds. The Council restored Bitcoin proof submissions on Nov. 7. The app reopened at about 03:00 UTC on Nov. 10. A review of 57 wallet addresses matched 31 redemption payouts to bridge proofs and found no unexplained outflows.
